caption: Figure 2. Visualizing how the BSGS algorithm [32] reduces the number of ciphertext rotations in matrix-vector products.
subject: how the baby-step giant-step (BSGS) algorithm regroups a matrix's diagonals to cut the number of ciphertext rotations needed for a homomorphic matrix-vector product

groups.why_chosen: Splitting an n x n matrix-vector product's n diagonals into n1 baby-step groups of n2 diagonals each cuts the needed ciphertext rotations from n down to about n1+n2 (here 3+2=5 vs 6), a saving that grows as O(sqrt(n)) instead of O(n) for larger matrices.
groups.what_to_learn: colour-banded diagonals of a matrix extracted into separate multiply-and-sum columns, regrouped by a rotation-count bracket label, to make an asymptotic rotation-count argument visually countable
